newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down but off lows on Monday on profit-taking in blue chips Telkom and Sampoerna and some small stocks, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.51 points, or 0.36 percent, to close at 692.50 points. Losers led gainers by 59 to 50, with 74 counters unchanged. Total turn-over was thin, estimated at 261 billion rupiah.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed in slow trading on Tuesday due to a lack of fresh leads as most of the major companies had already announced first quarter results.

They said the lack of overseas buyers due to a holiday in Hong Kong and generally weak regional markets had contributed to the sluggish trade in the local market despite strong rises in the Dow Jones industrial average on Friday.
"Some foreign investors who left Indonesia market due to (last month's) general election have not started coming back yet," one analyst with a foreign firm said.

The analyst predicted that in the short-term, local investors would dominate trading with the focus on selected small stocks which are the subject of rumours such as stock splits, bonus shares and new joint ventures.
"Local-led buyers will keep their eye on cheap stocks," the analyst said, referring to Apac Centertex, Ever Shine Tex and Polysindo.
Shoe-maker Kasogi International, Modern Bank and small paper company Suparma were among the targets of buyers on talks of stock splits and bonus shares, brokers said.
Large profit-taking was seen on travel and tourism firm Bayu Buana after reports that its first quarter net profit was 102 percent higher than the same 1996 period.
"Its a little bit strange but that's how it is ... investors buy on rumours and then sell on confirmed news," one local broker said.
Bayu was the most active stock with 12.1 million shares traded, falling 100 rupiah to 1,400 rupiah.
Blue chips Bank Negara Indonesia, Telkom and Sampoerna were among the losers on profit-taking, brokers said.
